video:
Vertical short (9:16), about 60 seconds (the voice settings' length wins). Write in the scenes format: `## Beat` headings, spoken lines, one `Visual: TYPE | fields` per beat. The beats below are roles: name yours for their content ("How it moves", "The catch"), split any beat over ~15s, and treat the seconds as a guide.

## Hook (0–3s): the most surprising true thing, in the first five words. No greeting, no title card. Visual: stat, compare, or text.
## Stakes (3–10s): why it hits this viewer's money, time, safety, or plans. Open the question the video will answer. Visual: text, stat, or image.
## Substance 1 (10–25s): the first piece of the answer: what happened or how it works. Visual: list, compare, or timeline.
## Substance 2 (25–38s): re-hook with a turn ("But…", the catch, the next question), then the evidence. Visual: bars, compare, or stat.
## Substance 3 (38–50s, optional): the surprising consequence or the honest caveat. Visual: text, quote, or image.
## Payoff (50–57s): answer the opening question in one line worth remembering. Not a summary. Visual: text.
## End (57–60s): a short CTA; for Shorts and Reels, a last line that loops back into the hook. Visual: end.
post:
WhatsApp channel post, under 180 words, standalone.
*Bold hook line*: the surprising fact or the stake, not a label.
2–3 short paragraphs, one idea each; numbers and names, not adjectives.
_One-line takeaway_: what to do or remember.
Sources: 1–3 plain URLs. Emoji: one at most.
